name: Telescopic Lens
summary: Gazlowe needs the Telescopic Lens to finish the observatory telescope above Ratchet’s harbor. Southsea pirates took it from a ship, and the lens remains in their camp south of town.

sections.title: Eyes on the Sky
sections.body: Ratchet is known chiefly for ruthless commerce, but its overseer and chief engineer, Gazlowe, has greater mechanical ambitions. His observatory rises above the harbor to house a telescope for watching maritime traffic and the stars. The larger lens came safely overland from Durotar. The smaller, vital lens traveled by sea, where Southsea Freebooters prey on merchant lanes off the Barrens coast.

sections.title: Pirate Plunder
sections.body: The Southsea Freebooters took anything of value when they raided the transport ship, including the delicate optics. The pirates may have left the lens among the clutter of their beachside camp south of Ratchet because they could not appreciate its craft or did not know how to pawn it. Gazlowe needs the unblemished glass brought back so his observation deck can come into focus.

faq.q: Why does Gazlowe need this lens?
faq.answer: Gazlowe needs the Telescopic Lens to finish the telescope in Ratchet’s observatory. The larger lens arrived overland from Durotar, but the smaller lens was lost at sea.

Southsea Freebooters stole the Telescopic Lens. They are opportunistic human and goblin pirates who prey on merchant ships near the Merchant Coast, and they keep the lens in a marked crate at their coastal camp south of Ratchet.

faq.q: Where did the lens originally come from?
faq.answer: The Telescopic Lens was shipped by sea to Ratchet, while its counterpart came overland from Durotar. Inbound shipments to the port often come from across the Great Sea or from southern goblin holdings such as Booty Bay.

faq.q: Is the lens undamaged despite being stolen?
faq.answer: Miraculously, the lens survived unharmed. A crate marked “Fragile - Do Not Drop” protected the precision glass from the pirates’ rough handling.

angles.text: As an engineer, you can see the fine optical craft in this lens. It is needed to focus long-range observation mechanisms without spherical aberration.
As a gnome, you may scoff at goblin rocketry, but Gazlowe’s devotion to optical astronomy shows goblin engineering is not all about high explosives.
